# GOAL Produce a complete, primary-sourced reference inventory of Vietnam's past, present and future thermal generation assets (> 30 MWe). Begin the document directly with the inventory table — no title, no preamble, no overview section. Structure it as follows: - the plant inventory: **exactly one pipe table**, never split into sub-tables by status, fuel, province, or any other dimension. Columns in this exact order: Name (Vietnamese), Name (English), Province, Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG), Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas), Units × MW, Total MWe, Status, Status as-of-date, COD, Owner/Developer, Confidence, Source 1, Source 2, Notes. Do not add statistical summary, cross-tabulation, or any other pipe tables; fold aggregate statistics into prose. - per-asset or per-project explanatory notes: for each asset that warrants it (major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important), a concise sourced note covering development history, notable issues, and confidence-qualified attributes. Straightforward operational assets need no note. - an annotated bibliography of every source cited (full citation; URL when available; original-language title plus English translation for non-English sources; summary annotation of what was drawn from each) Scope includes all thermal assets > 30 MWe at any stage of the lifecycle, including shelved or cancelled projects. When uncertain, mark confidence LOW and explain why in the Notes field. Never fabricate sources or URLs; write "URL not verified" if you cannot locate the exact handle. Include known plants even without a primary source rather than omitting them. Output format: Markdown. # QUALITY DIMENSIONS Your output is judged on four axes: 1. *Accuracy* — right assets and right attributes. Row level: recall and precision against a curated reference (F1). Cell level: capacity, fuel, location, operator, COD, status correct. Confident fabrication is the policed failure mode. 2. *Coherence* — internally and externally consistent. Totals reconcile with known subtotals; no negative capacities, no double-counted units, no cross-row contradiction; values plausible in unit, magnitude, geography, technology, date. Conflicting sources reconciled explicitly (which chosen and why), not silently. 3. *Provenance* — each value traces to a source that actually supports it, not a merely plausible citation. Two independent primaries is the ideal; one primary, a regulator database, or a marked secondary is weaker but acceptable if its status is explicit. Unsupported values are the failure. 4. *Temporality* — every value carries a best-effort as-of date; status changes are flagged. Distinguish current status from past reports, planned from operating capacity, source date from fact date. We prefer a comprehensive inventory with uncertainty clearly expressed over a shortlist of well-known assets. # CONTEXT ## Source quality management Two distinct epistemic roles — do not conflate them: - Discovery & characterization: parametric knowledge and web search, including tertiary sources, MAY be used to generate leads, locate assets, and form initial hypotheses about attributes. - Justification in the final inventory: a claim can be justified ONLY by an admissible independently consulted source that actually supports it. Admissible primary sources: official government documents; regulator-aggregated official data; operator filings/press releases. Admissible secondary sources: international-institution reports; bylined trade press; industry trackers and data brokers that expose the primary they cite. Not admissible sources: - Tertiary compilations (encyclopedias, Wikipedia/Wikidata/DBpedia, mirrors, aggregators re-syndicating without independent verification). - Any deposited dataset that does NOT expose, per value, the primary source it draws from — a DOI or repository deposit does not by itself confer admissibility. Local-language sources are preferred but not required; when used, include the original-language title plus an English translation in brackets. If a lead surfaces only via an inadmissible source, trace to its original source and cite that; if none is found, record Source = "not found", confidence LOW. In the table mention the inadmissible source in Notes, not in Sources. ## Calibrated confidence vocabulary Each row in the inventory table carries a confidence level based on evidence and agreement: - HIGH = >=2 INDEPENDENT concordant sources, at least one is primary - MEDIUM = 1 primary source, OR a sourced aggregator citing a verifiable primary - LOW = secondary only / inferred / unresolved conflict / not found Independence check (run BEFORE judging agreement): - Trace each source to its origin; merge sources sharing one origin into ONE. - Sources re-syndicating Wikipedia/Wikidata are NOT independent and NOT admissible. - Filling both Source columns does not by itself confer HIGH; independence is required Hard ceilings (override the above): - Commercial operator self-reported not confirmed by an official source: cap claim at MEDIUM. - Status attested only by a source older than 24 months and unconfirmed since: cap status at MEDIUM (LOW if older than 48 months). Freshness is measured on the publication date of the most recent admissible source attesting the status — NOT on the older Status as-of-date. - "Source = not found" rows: LOW by construction. Explanatory notes must state the confidence level for the row-level existence/status claim and may additionally qualify one or two disputed attributes (capacity, status, fuel, COD, owner/operator, or location). Per qualified claim, state: value, confidence level, evidence type (primary/secondary), and sources. When sources disagree, investigate for transcription errors, time-based changes, and unit/translation issues; follow the higher-tier source if unresolved, and add a note in the Notes cell. ## Asset-row and status rules Each row corresponds to one asset record. The DEFAULT unit is the plant / unit-group, not the power center: when a site co-locates several plants with distinct capacity, COD, owner/developer, fuel, status, or financing (BOT/IPP) arrangements, each one is its own row. Aggregate to center-level in a single row ONLY when detailed evidence is unavailable; in that case mark the row ambiguous and explain the aggregation in Notes. Conversely, do not split a single plant into multiple rows when the only difference is individual generating units sharing one commissioning, owner, and status — record these as Units × MW on one row. Status definitions (use these exact terms, aligned with Global Energy Monitor vocabulary): - Announced: described in government plans or corporate filings; no permits sought, no land acquired. - Pre-permit: environmental and regulatory approvals being sought; no permits issued yet. - Permitted: all required government approvals received; construction not yet started. - Construction: site preparation or EPC execution underway. - Operating: formally commissioned. - Shelved: previously active or advancing but progress halted without formal cancellation. - Cancelled: formally cancelled or replaced by another project. - Retired: permanently closed or decommissioned. Capacity rule: Record nameplate electrical capacity in MWe when available. If sources do not distinguish gross vs net, record the stated MW value and note "gross/net unspecified". Do not mix thermal MW, boiler capacity, steam output, or investment package capacity with electrical MWe. For Units × MW, make arithmetic consistent with Total MWe or explain discrepancies in Notes. Explanatory notes discipline: The table comes first. Per-asset notes follow the table and are selective: write one only for assets that are major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important. For straightforward operational assets a compact Notes cell in the table is sufficient; do not repeat it as a separate note. # Evidence pack These are manually curated primary sources meant to boost but not replace your own deep research. 1. evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities — EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 2. evn_ar_2017_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2017 3. evn_ar_2018_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2018 4. pdp7a_annex1_table1 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 5. pdp7a_annex1_table2 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 6. pdp7a_annex1_table3 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 7. pdp7_annex1 — PDP7 Annex I 8. pdp7_annex2 — PDP7 Annex II 9. pdp8_annex2_table1 — PDP8 Annex II 10. pdp8_annex2_table2 — PDP8 Annex II 11. pdp8_annex2_table3 — PDP8 Annex II 12. pdp8_annex2_table4 — PDP8 Annex II 13. pdp8_annex2_table5 — PDP8 Annex II 14. report_32_annex1 — Report 32 Annex 1 15. report_58_annex — Report 58 Annex 16. study_e542_pl9_1 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 17. study_e542_pl9_2 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 18. study_e542_pl9_5a — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex ## Chunk 1 source_id: evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities file: EVN_Annual_Report_2010_2011_CapacitiesTable.md document_title: EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 section_title: Corporate overview - installed capacity of power plants as of 31/12/2011 source_type: operator annual report table extract relevance: Installed-capacity and owner baseline from EVN for the 2011 system, including thermal plants alongside other generation types <<>> # EVN Annual Report 2010-2011, pp 13-14 ## Corporate overview ### Công suất đặt các nhà máy điện tính tới 31/12/2011

The inventory contains approximately 90 discrete asset records spanning the full lifecycle of Vietnam's thermal generation fleet. In aggregate, the operating coal fleet totals roughly 25,000–27,000 MWe (consistent with the approximately 28,000 MW reported at end-2025 by Vietnamese media, which includes some plants not individually confirmed here such as smaller TKV units). By the end of 2025, the country's total installed power capacity had reached about 88,000 MW, with coal-fired power accounting for nearly 28,000 MW, or more than 30 per cent of the total. The operating domestic-gas CCGT fleet totals approximately 7,500–8,000 MWe (Phú Mỹ complex, Nhơn Trạch 1-2, Cà Mau 1-2, Bà Rịa), and with a total capacity of 1,624 MW, the Nhơn Trạch 3 and Nhơn Trạch 4 power plants added Vietnam's first LNG capacity in late 2025. Under PDP8, approximately 22,400 MW of LNG-fired capacity and roughly 7,600 MW of domestic-gas CCGT capacity are planned for 2021–2030, though many projects lack confirmed developers or depend on upstream gas-field timelines (Lô B, Cá Voi Xanh, Báo Vàng). Regarding coal power, by 2030, the total capacity of operating plants and projects under construction is expected to be completed and put into operation at about 31,055 MW, with five coal projects (4,360 MW) to be urgently completed and 3 projects/5,300 MW (Nam Dinh I, Song Hau II, Vinh Tan 3) facing difficulties in arranging capital and changing investor structure. By 2050, the orientation is to no longer use coal for electricity generation, completely switching to using biomass/ammonia.

## Per-Asset Explanatory Notes

### Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4 (LNG CCGT, 2 × 812 MW, Đồng Nai)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, status, capacity, COD).** Vietnam's first LNG-fired power complex. Invested by Vietnam Oil and Gas Power Corporation (PV Power), a member unit of Petrovietnam, with the Lilama–Samsung C&T consortium as the EPC general contractor. The Project consists of two gas-fired power plants using LNG with total capacity of 1624MW. The plants will be equipped with GE's 50Hz, 9HA.02 gas turbines fuelled by LNG. Construction began in 2022 after PM investment approval in 2019. Nhon Trach 3 Power Plant had its completion acceptance approved by the State Council in October 2025 and was granted COD status on November 20, 2025. On December 3, 2025, the Nhon Trach 4 Project completed state-level acceptance testing and is expected to complete the COD certification on December 20, 2025. PDP7A had planned the Nhơn Trạch 3&4 complex (as 2×750 MW) for 2020–2021; actual COD was delayed roughly 4–5 years.

### Thái Bình II (Coal, 2 × 600 MW, Thái Bình)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, status); MEDIUM (technology).** The Thái Bình 2 thermal power plant, operated by PetroVietnam, consists in two 600 MW supercritical coal-fired units. The plant is located next to the Thái Bình 1 thermal power plant, comprised of two 300 MW subcritical anthracite units, commissioned in 2017 and 2018. PDP7A had planned COD 2017–2018 for Thái Bình II. The project was severely delayed due to legal/corruption issues and the COVID-19 pandemic. The project's development was eventful, especially at times when the project came to a grinding halt as past issues led to challenges in legal and funding matters. Inaugurated April 2023.

### Long Phú I (Coal, 2 × 600 MW, Sóc Trăng)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (existence, capacity); LOW (COD, status).** Long Phu 1 is a 1.2GW supercritical thermal power plant being developed in the Long Phu district of Soc Trang Province. EPC by consortium of Power Machines (Russia), BTG Holding (Slovakia), and PTSC. The project is expected to face a delay of 36 months compared with original plans after the US Treasury put Power Machines in an embargo list. Construction was approximately 78% complete as of 2020 per E-542 study, but has been largely suspended since. As of March 2024, the proposed loan financing arrangements appeared to not be going ahead. As of March 2025, there was no further news on financing the project. PDP8 revised lists COD 2027 but this remains highly uncertain.

### Vũng Áng II (Coal, 2 × 665 MW, Hà Tĩnh)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, construction status); MEDIUM (COD).** BOT project. The Vung Ang II Thermal Power Plant (VAPCO) project, which commenced construction in 2021, has a total investment of US$2.2 billion and comprises two units with a total capacity of over 1,200 MW. The Vung Ang II Thermal Power Plant utilizes ultra-supercritical (USC) boiler technology – considered by experts to be the most advanced technology for coal-fired power plants in Vietnam. PDP8 lists 1,330 MW (nameplate higher than original 2×600 plan). PDP8 revised lists COD 2025–2026. Included in MoF September 2025 BOT tax exemption proposal, suggesting advanced commissioning.

### Quảng Trạch I (Coal, 2 × ~700 MW, Quảng Bình)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, construction); MEDIUM (capacity, COD).** Originally planned as 2×600 MW under PVN (PDP7A). Transferred to EVN. PDP8 lists capacity as 1,403 MW—higher than earlier 1,200 MW plans, suggesting uprated turbines. As of February 2024, construction was expected to be 61% complete by the end of the year. As of March 2024, Unit 1 was expected to begin operating in May 2026, and Unit 2 in October 2026. Report 32 estimated COD 2024 (delayed 2.5 years from PDP7A plan); further delays have pushed to 2026.

### Vân Phong I (Coal BOT, 2 × 716 MW, Khánh Hòa)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (status, COD).** Sumitomo BOT project. PDP8 lists 1,432 MW under construction. E-542 study (Nov 2020) stated PPA signed, with COD estimated mid-2023 + early 2024. PDP8 revised lists COD 2024. Included in MoF September 2025 BOT tax exemption proposal alongside confirmed-operating BOTs (Nghi Sơn II, Mông Dương II, etc.), strongly implying the plant is now operating. Technology likely USC (modern large-scale BOT) but not confirmed in primary sources.

### Sông Hậu II (Coal BOT, 2 × 1,000+ MW, Hậu Giang)

**Confidence: HIGH (cancelled status).** Malaysian developer Toyo Ink/Toyo Ventures held the BOT contract. PDP8 Table 3 listed it as delayed (2,120 MW). In January 2025, Toyo Ventures officially disputed MOIT's contract termination. The BOT contract was terminated by MOIT in July 2024. The project's future is unclear amid ongoing legal dispute.

### Vĩnh Tân III (Coal BOT, 3 × 660 MW, Bình Thuận)

**Confidence: HIGH (shelved status).** Originally a BOT with VTEC (consortium including Mitsubishi, One Energy). In February 2021 Mitsubishi announced that it was withdrawing from Vinh Tan-3, the first time Mitsubishi has withdrawn from a coal plant project. Mitsubishi cited its climate targets as the main reason. PDP8 Table 3 lists it among delayed/troubled projects. PDP8 revised retains it among projects "facing difficulties in arranging capital."

### Ô Môn Complex (Gas CCGT, Cần Thơ)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** The Ô Môn power center is planned to host four gas-fired units using domestic gas from the Lô B offshore field (Block B, Ô Môn gas pipeline). Ô Môn I (660 MW, existing oil-fired) is to convert to gas; Ô Môn II, III, IV (each 1,050 MW CCGT per PDP8) are new-build. All timelines depend on the Lô B gas field development. Reports 32 and 58 note 3–5 year delays, with synchronization to Lô B as the binding constraint. PDP8 Table 5 lists all four as planned for 2021–2030 but without specific COD dates.

### Dung Quất / Miền Trung Complex (Domestic Gas CCGT, Quảng Ngãi / Quảng Trị)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** Five CCGT plants (Dung Quất I-III, Miền Trung I-II, each 750 MW per PDP8 Table 5) are planned to use gas from the Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore field operated by ExxonMobil. All are contingent on the CVX field reaching final investment decision and gas delivery. Report 58 estimated COD 2024–2026 for various units but noted "đồng bộ khí CVX" (synchronized with CVX gas) as the key constraint.

### LNG Bạc Liêu (3,200 MW, Bạc Liêu)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (existence in plan); LOW (implementation feasibility).** PDP8 Table 1 lists 3,200 MW for 2021–2030. The project was first added to the revised PDP7 as a large LNG scheme, with pre-feasibility underway as of 2020 per E-542. No confirmed developer or EPC contract in primary sources.

The inventory contains approximately 90 discrete asset records spanning the full lifecycle of Vietnam's thermal generation fleet. In aggregate, the operating coal fleet totals roughly 25,000–27,000 MWe (consistent with the approximately 28,000 MW reported at end-2025 by Vietnamese media, which includes some plants not individually confirmed here such as smaller TKV units). By the end of 2025, the country's total installed power capacity had reached about 88,000 MW, with coal-fired power accounting for nearly 28,000 MW, or more than 30 per cent of the total. The operating domestic-gas CCGT fleet totals approximately 7,500–8,000 MWe (Phú Mỹ complex, Nhơn Trạch 1-2, Cà Mau 1-2, Bà Rịa), and with a total capacity of 1,624 MW, the Nhơn Trạch 3 and Nhơn Trạch 4 power plants added Vietnam's first LNG capacity in late 2025. Under PDP8, approximately 22,400 MW of LNG-fired capacity and roughly 7,600 MW of domestic-gas CCGT capacity are planned for 2021–2030, though many projects lack confirmed developers or depend on upstream gas-field timelines (Lô B, Cá Voi Xanh, Báo Vàng). Regarding coal power, by 2030, the total capacity of operating plants and projects under construction is expected to be completed and put into operation at about 31,055 MW, with five coal projects (4,360 MW) to be urgently completed and 3 projects/5,300 MW (Nam Dinh I, Song Hau II, Vinh Tan 3) facing difficulties in arranging capital and changing investor structure. By 2050, the orientation is to no longer use coal for electricity generation, completely switching to using biomass/ammonia.

## Per-Asset Explanatory Notes

### Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4 (LNG CCGT, 2 × 812 MW, Đồng Nai)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, status, capacity, COD).** Vietnam's first LNG-fired power complex. Invested by Vietnam Oil and Gas Power Corporation (PV Power), a member unit of Petrovietnam, with the Lilama–Samsung C&T consortium as the EPC general contractor. The Project consists of two gas-fired power plants using LNG with total capacity of 1624MW. The plants will be equipped with GE's 50Hz, 9HA.02 gas turbines fuelled by LNG. Construction began in 2022 after PM investment approval in 2019. Nhon Trach 3 Power Plant had its completion acceptance approved by the State Council in October 2025 and was granted COD status on November 20, 2025. On December 3, 2025, the Nhon Trach 4 Project completed state-level acceptance testing and is expected to complete the COD certification on December 20, 2025. PDP7A had planned the Nhơn Trạch 3&4 complex (as 2×750 MW) for 2020–2021; actual COD was delayed roughly 4–5 years.

### Thái Bình II (Coal, 2 × 600 MW, Thái Bình)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, status); MEDIUM (technology).** The Thái Bình 2 thermal power plant, operated by PetroVietnam, consists in two 600 MW supercritical coal-fired units. The plant is located next to the Thái Bình 1 thermal power plant, comprised of two 300 MW subcritical anthracite units, commissioned in 2017 and 2018. PDP7A had planned COD 2017–2018 for Thái Bình II. The project was severely delayed due to legal/corruption issues and the COVID-19 pandemic. The project's development was eventful, especially at times when the project came to a grinding halt as past issues led to challenges in legal and funding matters. Inaugurated April 2023.

### Long Phú I (Coal, 2 × 600 MW, Sóc Trăng)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (existence, capacity); LOW (COD, status).** Long Phu 1 is a 1.2GW supercritical thermal power plant being developed in the Long Phu district of Soc Trang Province. EPC by consortium of Power Machines (Russia), BTG Holding (Slovakia), and PTSC. The project is expected to face a delay of 36 months compared with original plans after the US Treasury put Power Machines in an embargo list. Construction was approximately 78% complete as of 2020 per E-542 study, but has been largely suspended since. As of March 2024, the proposed loan financing arrangements appeared to not be going ahead. As of March 2025, there was no further news on financing the project. PDP8 revised lists COD 2027 but this remains highly uncertain.

### Vũng Áng II (Coal, 2 × 665 MW, Hà Tĩnh)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, construction status); MEDIUM (COD).** BOT project. The Vung Ang II Thermal Power Plant (VAPCO) project, which commenced construction in 2021, has a total investment of US$2.2 billion and comprises two units with a total capacity of over 1,200 MW. The Vung Ang II Thermal Power Plant utilizes ultra-supercritical (USC) boiler technology – considered by experts to be the most advanced technology for coal-fired power plants in Vietnam. PDP8 lists 1,330 MW (nameplate higher than original 2×600 plan). PDP8 revised lists COD 2025–2026. Included in MoF September 2025 BOT tax exemption proposal, suggesting advanced commissioning.

### Quảng Trạch I (Coal, 2 × ~700 MW, Quảng Bình)

**Confidence: HIGH (existence, construction); MEDIUM (capacity, COD).** Originally planned as 2×600 MW under PVN (PDP7A). Transferred to EVN. PDP8 lists capacity as 1,403 MW—higher than earlier 1,200 MW plans, suggesting uprated turbines. As of February 2024, construction was expected to be 61% complete by the end of the year. As of March 2024, Unit 1 was expected to begin operating in May 2026, and Unit 2 in October 2026. Report 32 estimated COD 2024 (delayed 2.5 years from PDP7A plan); further delays have pushed to 2026.

### Vân Phong I (Coal BOT, 2 × 716 MW, Khánh Hòa)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (status, COD).** Sumitomo BOT project. PDP8 lists 1,432 MW under construction. E-542 study (Nov 2020) stated PPA signed, with COD estimated mid-2023 + early 2024. PDP8 revised lists COD 2024. Included in MoF September 2025 BOT tax exemption proposal alongside confirmed-operating BOTs (Nghi Sơn II, Mông Dương II, etc.), strongly implying the plant is now operating. Technology likely USC (modern large-scale BOT) but not confirmed in primary sources.

### Sông Hậu II (Coal BOT, 2 × 1,000+ MW, Hậu Giang)

**Confidence: HIGH (cancelled status).** Malaysian developer Toyo Ink/Toyo Ventures held the BOT contract. PDP8 Table 3 listed it as delayed (2,120 MW). In January 2025, Toyo Ventures officially disputed MOIT's contract termination. The BOT contract was terminated by MOIT in July 2024. The project's future is unclear amid ongoing legal dispute.

### Vĩnh Tân III (Coal BOT, 3 × 660 MW, Bình Thuận)

**Confidence: HIGH (shelved status).** Originally a BOT with VTEC (consortium including Mitsubishi, One Energy). In February 2021 Mitsubishi announced that it was withdrawing from Vinh Tan-3, the first time Mitsubishi has withdrawn from a coal plant project. Mitsubishi cited its climate targets as the main reason. PDP8 Table 3 lists it among delayed/troubled projects. PDP8 revised retains it among projects "facing difficulties in arranging capital."

### Ô Môn Complex (Gas CCGT, Cần Thơ)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** The Ô Môn power center is planned to host four gas-fired units using domestic gas from the Lô B offshore field (Block B, Ô Môn gas pipeline). Ô Môn I (660 MW, existing oil-fired) is to convert to gas; Ô Môn II, III, IV (each 1,050 MW CCGT per PDP8) are new-build. All timelines depend on the Lô B gas field development. Reports 32 and 58 note 3–5 year delays, with synchronization to Lô B as the binding constraint. PDP8 Table 5 lists all four as planned for 2021–2030 but without specific COD dates.

### Dung Quất / Miền Trung Complex (Domestic Gas CCGT, Quảng Ngãi / Quảng Trị)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** Five CCGT plants (Dung Quất I-III, Miền Trung I-II, each 750 MW per PDP8 Table 5) are planned to use gas from the Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore field operated by ExxonMobil. All are contingent on the CVX field reaching final investment decision and gas delivery. Report 58 estimated COD 2024–2026 for various units but noted "đồng bộ khí CVX" (synchronized with CVX gas) as the key constraint.

### LNG Bạc Liêu (3,200 MW, Bạc Liêu)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (existence in plan); LOW (implementation feasibility).** PDP8 Table 1 lists 3,200 MW for 2021–2030. The project was first added to the revised PDP7 as a large LNG scheme, with pre-feasibility underway as of 2020 per E-542. No confirmed developer or EPC contract in primary sources.

### Ô Môn Complex (Gas CCGT, Cần Thơ)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** The Ô Môn power center is planned to host four gas-fired units using domestic gas from the Lô B offshore field (Block B, Ô Môn gas pipeline). Ô Môn I (660 MW, existing oil-fired) is to convert to gas; Ô Môn II, III, IV (each 1,050 MW CCGT per PDP8) are new-build. All timelines depend on the Lô B gas field development. Reports 32 and 58 note 3–5 year delays, with synchronization to Lô B as the binding constraint. PDP8 Table 5 lists all four as planned for 2021–2030 but without specific COD dates.

### Dung Quất / Miền Trung Complex (Domestic Gas CCGT, Quảng Ngãi / Quảng Trị)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (planned status); LOW (COD).** Five CCGT plants (Dung Quất I-III, Miền Trung I-II, each 750 MW per PDP8 Table 5) are planned to use gas from the Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore field operated by ExxonMobil. All are contingent on the CVX field reaching final investment decision and gas delivery. Report 58 estimated COD 2024–2026 for various units but noted "đồng bộ khí CVX" (synchronized with CVX gas) as the key constraint.

### LNG Bạc Liêu (3,200 MW, Bạc Liêu)

**Confidence: MEDIUM (existence in plan); LOW (implementation feasibility).** PDP8 Table 1 lists 3,200 MW for 2021–2030. The project was first added to the revised PDP7 as a large LNG scheme, with pre-feasibility underway as of 2020 per E-542. No confirmed developer or EPC contract in primary sources.
